title: Dock+Puck
slugLine: A bedside sleep companion concept for Belkin with a removable puck, so people who travel often can take their wind-down routine with them.

figure.alt: Render of Dock+Puck: a white puck tilted open on a metal hinge above a base with a warm glowing light band and a grey fabric speaker.

research.problem: Working adults who travel often ==do not feel well rested== even after sleeping enough hours, because **their wind-down routine is disrupted the moment they leave home**.

stakeholders.name: Frequent travelers
stakeholders.note: Working adults, 25–40, who travel for work and leisure

painPoints.label: A disrupted wind-down
painPoints.detail: They cannot sleep comfortably because their wind-down routine is disrupted the moment they leave home.

painPoints.label: A shifting schedule
painPoints.detail: Their sleep schedule shifts every time they travel for business or leisure.

painPoints.label: Unfamiliar rooms
painPoints.detail: Testers named falling asleep and staying asleep in unfamiliar sleep environments as their main challenges.

painPoints.label: Screens before bed
painPoints.detail: They rack up high daily screen time, and screen use before bed makes it harder to fall asleep.

insights.evidence: A tester who travels six times a year found the scent feature useful for creating a familiar sleep environment.

insights.insight: The light helps waking more than winding down
insights.evidence: One tester said the light seems to help with waking up but not with winding down. Another valued it as a sunrise alarm.
Testers found the toggle controls unclear and, beyond the on/off button and the adaptive light, could not tell what the other features were.

insights.insight: It needs to be smaller to travel
insights.evidence: Testers said it takes up too much desk space and asked for a smaller, more portable form.

design.lead: The final concept pairs a magnetic charging dock with a removable sleep puck. At home it is one bedside device for light, sound and charging. On the road the puck comes along, and the routine comes with it.

blocks.title: Design criteria
items: Aids physical and mental relaxation with multi-sensory features

blocks.title: An earlier concept: Sleep Plane
items: A charging dock, adaptive light and sleep speaker
Its width and depth took up too much desk space
It offered too few features for its size

rows.label: Charging dock
cells: Magnetic wireless charging dock for the puck and phone
Keeps the bedside setup simple and cuts extra cables during the wind-down routine

rows.label: Adaptive light
cells: Adjustable brightness and color temperature with simple touch or physical controls
Smooths the move from wakefulness to sleep with a calming bedside environment

rows.label: Sleep speaker
cells: Adjustable volume with simple physical controls for white noise, calming sounds and alarms
Creates a consistent sleep environment without headphones or earbuds

rows.label: Portable puck
cells: A removable, compact sleep module that works apart from the dock
Makes the sleep setup easy to bring when traveling or moving between rooms

image.alt: Dock+Puck on a wooden bedside table in a dim bedroom, its base glowing warm, with a phone on the puck showing 12:50.

blocks.title: Medium-fidelity prototype

image.alt: A handmade prototype in cardboard and white paper: a round base with a cardboard puck tilted up on top.

blocks.caption: The medium-fidelity prototype used in user testing.

results.lead: Five frequent travelers tested the medium-fidelity prototype, and their feedback set ==three priority iterations== for the next round.

rows.label: Gen Z woman, 6 trips a year
cells: Falling asleep in unfamiliar sleep environments
The scent feature, for a familiar sleep environment
Simpler physical controls that are easier to understand at night

rows.label: Millennial man, 5 trips a year
cells: The light seems to help with waking up
It does not help winding down, and takes up too much desk space

rows.label: Gen Z woman, 3 trips a year
cells: The design looks futuristic and aesthetic
Beyond the on/off button and adaptive light, the features are not clear

rows.label: Millennial woman, 2 trips a year
cells: Wireless charging and the light; a sunrise alarm helps her wake up
The toggle controls are not clear

rows.label: Gen Z man, 2 trips a year
cells: Falling asleep, screen use before bed
Combining speaker, light and scent in one product
A smaller, more portable form for travel

blocks.title: Priority iterations
items: Reduce the overall size of the product
Add icons or visual aids that show each feature and what it does
